Grimes). extracted text of PDF p. 102 (printed p. 94, Appendix E 'Comparative word lists', 'Symbols' box) gives, exactly as quoted: 'Stress in South Sulawesi languages usually occurs on the penultimate syllable. In such cases it is not marked in the word lists. Where stress deviates from the normal pattern or where stress may be unclear due to double vocoids, etc., it is marked with an apostrophe preceding the stressed syllable.' Verbatim (only scanned letter-spacing differs). I re-rendered PDF p. 146 (printed p. 138) at 110 dpi: row CAM, item 80…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the penultimate syllable. The statement is made for the South Sulawesi languages as a group, on the basis of the authors' own 1982-83 survey wordlists; Campalagian is one of those lists and its ~200 forms are left unmarked (= penultimate) except one, 'far' mala'taa (p. 138), where the mark falls on a final double-vocoid syllable, the 'unclear' case the convention allows for.
new_statements.exceptions: General: deviation from the penultimate pattern and unclear stress on double vocoids are marked with an apostrophe. Selayar (not Campalagian) is singled out for antepenultimate stress in some words (p. 96). For Campalagian only mala'taa 'far' is marked.
new_statements.domain_note: Citation forms from an elicited wordlist (isolated words, some two-word items); no statement about phrase-level stress, clitics or suffixed forms. Family-level generalization, not a Campalagian-specific phonological description.
new_statements.identity_note: Grimes & Grimes 1987 treat Campalagian (alt. Tallumpanuae, Tasing, Tjampalagian) as a language distinct from Bugis within a 'Bugis Family' (61% lexical similarity), i.e. the same entity as Glottolog camp1262; their CAM list comes from the town of Campalagian, Kab. Polewali Mandar (informant Darwis). Muthalib & Usmar call it 'dialek Tallumpanuane/Campalagian' (Bugis dialect framing), same variety.
